question: Do public NCBI sequence records provide specimen metadata for the Pantabangan fish-barcode lead, and are they demonstrably the accessions used by the 2026 journal article?

query.method: NCBI E-utilities Nucleotide search with Pantabangan[All Fields], followed by GenBank-format retrieval for all returned NCBI record IDs. A fish-project subset was identified by the exact GenBank REFERENCE 1 title, not by locality text alone.
limitations: The text search is a discovery query, not a spatial or validated waterbody filter.
The GenBank project title alone is not used as a substitute for row-level geo_loc_name; one fish record is only localized to Nueva Ecija.
The EFetch file contains nucleotide sequences and is retained only in the ignored local raw directory; no sequence strings are embedded in this review.

excludedIndexMatches.definition: Hipposideros obscurus voucher MRMD1155 cytochrome oxidase subunit 1 (COI) gene, partial cds; mitochondrial.
excludedIndexMatches.disposition: Excluded from the fish-project subset because the NCBI result is not linked to the Pantabangan fish-project reference title.

historicalPublishedCrosswalk.result: The 2015 paper's range resolves to exactly five GenBank records. Their submitted organism is Clarias batrachus, their specimen vouchers are PNT-14, PNT-02, PNT-17, PNT-16, and PNT-15, and all five NCBI geo_loc_name fields explicitly include Pantabangan Dam. This verifies a historical accession crosswalk for that five-record subset only.
limits: The accession-to-paper crosswalk does not independently validate voucher custody, specimen diagnosis, or current nomenclature.
It does not show that these five, or the other 35 records, are the exact dataset analyzed in the 2026 article.
These are a single historical sequence sample set used in related analyses, not five independent confirmations of present-day occurrence.

abstractNameOverlap: Micropterus floridanus (NCBI annotation: Micropterus salmoides floridanus)
comparisonWith2026Article.interpretation: The matching 40-record/nine-name totals, shared names, and overlapping authors/title are a strong discovery lead, and the five Clarias accessions are confirmed as having been analyzed in the separate 2015 Clarias paper. The NCBI records cite an unpublished project submitted in 2013, before the 2026 journal article was received in 2025. The 2026 abstract does not expose accession IDs, so the exact 2026 article sequence set remains unverified; do not extend the five-accession 2015 crosswalk to all 40 records.

findings.disposition: Historical accession-level evidence for an NCBI-submitted Pantabangan fish-barcode project. The 39 explicitly waterbody-localized records and one province-only fish record remain research-only; no species app assertion, sequence redistribution, diet statement, abundance estimate, current-presence claim, or regional release is approved.
findings.reuse: Public NCBI sequence records were retrieved for research review. No separate determination of application redistribution rights was made. Keep nucleotide sequences local and ignored; require taxonomy, source-lineage, and reuse review before any public projection.

nextStep: Obtain or locate the full 2026 article/supplement and compare its accession table to the 2013 NCBI submissions. Keep the source datasets separate until an exact crosswalk is documented; then review current taxonomy and reuse terms before deciding on any public species record.
